items.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Fitness Methods on Depressive Symptoms and Glycaemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Comorbid Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Taijiquan and Baduanjin.
items.authors: Tian X, Wei Y, Bo J, Lin K, Shen Y, Liu Y.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

abstract.text:
To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.

RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.

Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.

This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.

The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

items.title: More Than One Voice: Strengthening Organizational Readiness for Lived Experience Integration in Early Psychosis Services.
items.authors: Hayes SL, Sanford KC, Dauterive A, Jones NR, Pagdon S, McSweeney MF, Lumaquin J, Savill M, Niendam T.
items.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

sections.text: Knowledge derived from personal experience of mental health service use, by way of individuals with lived and living experience, is increasingly incorporated into mental health programs. Yet organizational readiness to support meaningful integration often lags behind intent. This paper offers a case analysis of the first 2 years of a Lived Experience Integration (LEI) Team embedded within a statewide early psychosis training and technical assistance network. Using Organizational Readiness for Change as a conceptual framework, this paper describes how leadership from people with lived experience contributed to training development, consultation, advisory structures, and workforce design, while navigating evolving infrastructure and the relational and interpretive demands of lived experience roles. Practical lessons are highlighted for building readiness to support durable lived experience integration in complex service systems. Lived Experience or Public Contribution: This manuscript describes work that was initiated and led with substantial involvement from individuals with lived experience of psychosis-spectrum conditions and mental health service use. Lived experience-identified contributors built the LEI Team under discussion, participated in consultation and training activities, advised on organizational tensions described in this case analysis, and were fully responsible for the conceptualization and writing of this manuscript.

items.title: Establishing the Structural Validity, Language-Based Performance, and Convergent Validity of the Caregiver Strain Questionnaire-Short Form 11 Within a Latinx Sample.
items.authors: Vázquez AL, Navarro Flores CM, Domenech Rodríguez MM, Held ML, Venta A, Moreno O, Galvan T, Perez Rojas OF, Cadenas GA.

sections.text: Caregiver strain or stress resulting from caring for a child with emotional/behavioral problems-can negatively impact the psychological health of caregivers and may underly decisions to seek mental health services for their youth. The Caregiver Strain Questionnaire-Short Form 11 (CGSQ-SF11) was developed to assess caregiver strain, but a Spanish language form has yet to be evaluated, limiting its utility with Latinx families. This study evaluated the CGSQ-SF11 as a tool for assessing caregiver strain among Latinx caregivers. The sample included 511 Latinx caregivers of youths aged 6-18 who self-selected into English (n = 275) or Spanish (n = 236) questionnaires. In general, caregivers reported moderate levels of caregiver strain, and caregivers who completed the Spanish survey reported significantly lower youth mental health problem severity and caregiver strain relative to those in the English survey. Confirmatory factor analyses suggest that a three-factor structure fit the data better (i.e., objective, subjective internalized, and subjective externalized strain) than a global factor. However, a bifactor model suggested that the variance in the total score was best represented by a unidimensional structure. The CGSQ-SF11 achieved metric invariance, which suggests that the latent variable and strength of factor loadings for the global scale were similar across language forms. Finally, we provide evidence of convergent validity through associations between the CGSQ-SF11 global scale and measures of youth internalizing and externalizing problems. Our findings support the use of CGSQ-SF11 English and Spanish language forms with Latinx caregivers.

items.title: Bioinformatics Analysis to Reveal Potential Targets of Huntington's Disease.
items.authors: Yang S, Xu X, Liu W, Zhang S.

sections.text: Huntington's disease (HD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease resulted from the expansion of CAG repeats in huntingtin (HTT) gene and characterised by motor impairment, psychiatric disorders and cognitive decline. Currently, there are no available disease-modifying treatments. In this study, we performed an integrative analysis of HD datasets downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database using machine learning approaches, Mendelian randomisation (MR) and single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis to elucidate underlying disease mechanisms. The machine learning algorithms of LASSO, random forest and SVM-RFE identified the decreased ADRA2A in HD. In addition, MR analysis revealed HD-associated proteins such as LILRA4 and UBE2D1, associated with immune response and ubiquitination metabolism, respectively. scRNA-seq analysis further identified the transcription factors of SOX4 and ETV1 through SCENIC analysis. Pseudotime trajectory analysis highlighted heparan sulphate sulfotransferase activity, involving genes CHST11, HS3ST3A1 and HS6ST3 that drive cell differentiation. Moreover, cell-cell communication analysis demonstrated enhanced NRG1/3-ERBB4 signalling pathway in HD. This study presents multiple potential targets for HD treatment but further experimental validation is required to confirm their functional relevance.
